narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 96% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. For an admissions decision, that is an extremely high risk signal, so the application was rejected.

The strongest factor was your third-year class-rank decile. Your value was 1.00, well below the average of about 5.79 among accepted students, and it pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The next most influential factor was your first-year class-rank decile: your value was 2.00 versus an accepted-student average of about 6.00, and it also pushed toward failure. Third was your LSAT score of 28, compared with an average of 37.18 among accepted students, which added further risk. In order, these academic indicators drove the denial.

To improve your chances, contact the admissions office for specific feedback and confirm the record is accurate. Then focus on the areas you can change: prepare for and retake the LSAT if possible, seek academic advising, and consider delaying reapplication until you have stronger evidence of bar-exam readiness. A structured study or readiness plan, plus a later application showing improvement, would give the committee a better basis to reconsider.
